name: Prague
tagline: A fairy-tale skyline of spires, castles and foaming Czech lager
description:
Prague looks like a city conjured from a storybook: a skyline of Gothic spires and Baroque domes, a castle sprawling along a ridge above the Vltava, and a 14th-century stone bridge lined with saints. Spared the worst destruction of the 20th century, its historic center is a remarkably intact museum of European architecture, from Romanesque cellars to Cubist lampposts and Art Nouveau cafés.

It is also a city of beer halls and hidden courtyards. Czechs drink more beer per person than anyone on earth, and a foaming half-liter of unpasteurized tank lager can cost less than a bottle of water in the tourist cafés. Step away from the Charles Bridge crowds and you'll find quiet passages, leafy hilltop parks and neighborhoods like Vinohrady and Holešovice, where cafés, galleries and beer gardens are packed with locals.

Visit early to have the bridge almost to yourself, climb Petřín Hill for sunset, and spend an evening at a classical concert in a candlelit church. Prague is compact, walkable and still good value, rewarding anyone willing to wander beyond the postcard views.

safety.notes: Prague is very safe when it comes to violent crime, but pickpockets work Charles Bridge, the Astronomical Clock crowds and tram 22. Dodgy exchange booths and unlicensed taxis are the city's most common tourist traps.

tipping: Round up or add about 10% at restaurants, telling the server the total you want to pay rather than leaving cash on the table.
gettingAround: Trams, metro and buses share one integrated ticket system, and the tram network covers the center brilliantly. The historic core is compact, so you'll walk most of the time; just watch your footing on the cobblestones.
tips: Skip street exchange booths advertising '0% commission'; withdraw koruna from bank ATMs and always choose to be charged in CZK rather than your home currency.
Cross Charles Bridge at sunrise for mist, soft light and almost nobody else around.
Prices on Old Town Square can be double those a few streets away, so walk five minutes before sitting down for a beer.
Tram 22 is a cheap sightseeing ride from the New Town past the National Theatre and up to Prague Castle.
Use a ride-hailing app or have your hotel call a taxi rather than hailing one on the street, where overcharging is common.
Buy transit tickets in the PID Lítačka app or at machines and validate paper tickets before boarding, as plain-clothes inspectors fine riders on the spot.
etiquette: Say 'dobrý den' when entering shops and restaurants and 'na shledanou' when you leave.
When toasting, say 'na zdraví' and look each person in the eye; skipping eye contact is said to bring bad luck.
Take off your shoes when entering someone's home, where slippers are usually provided.
Service can seem brusque, but it's efficiency rather than rudeness.

neighborhoods.name: Staré Město
neighborhoods.blurb: The Old Town's medieval maze of lanes, squares, churches and cellar bars around the Astronomical Clock.

neighborhoods.name: Malá Strana
neighborhoods.blurb: The Lesser Town below the castle, all Baroque palaces, gas lamps, hidden gardens and cozy pubs.

neighborhoods.name: Vinohrady
neighborhoods.blurb: An elegant residential district of Art Nouveau apartment blocks, leafy squares, wine bars and cafés.

neighborhoods.name: Žižkov
neighborhoods.blurb: Gritty, lively and famously packed with pubs, all beneath the city's space-age television tower.

neighborhoods.name: Holešovice
neighborhoods.blurb: A former industrial quarter reborn with contemporary galleries, a vast market hall and the leafy Letná beer garden.

dishes.name: Svíčková na smetaně
dishes.description: Marinated beef sirloin in a creamy root-vegetable sauce, served with bread dumplings, cranberries and a swirl of whipped cream.

dishes.name: Vepřo knedlo zelo
dishes.description: Roast pork, dumplings and sauerkraut, the holy trinity of Czech home cooking and the ultimate beer companion.

dishes.name: Smažený sýr
dishes.description: A thick slab of breaded, deep-fried cheese served with tartar sauce and fries, a much-loved guilty pleasure.

dishes.name: Chlebíčky
dishes.description: Dainty open-faced sandwiches topped with ham, egg, potato salad and pickles, perfect for a quick snack.

dishes.name: Tankové pivo
dishes.description: Unpasteurized lager delivered fresh to pubs in giant tanks and poured with a thick, creamy head of foam.

events.name: Prague Easter Markets
events.description: Old Town and Wenceslas squares fill with stalls selling painted eggs, wooden crafts, roast ham and warm drinks in the weeks around Easter.

events.name: Prague Spring International Music Festival
events.description: One of Europe's great classical music festivals opens on May 12 with Smetana's symphonic cycle Má vlast and runs into early June.

events.name: Signal Festival
events.description: For four October nights, video-mapping projections and light installations transform the city's façades and streets.

events.name: Prague Christmas Markets
events.description: Twinkling wooden stalls, a towering tree and mulled wine turn Old Town Square into a winter wonderland from late November.

attractions.name: Prague Castle
attractions.description: One of the largest castle complexes in the world stretches along a ridge above the river, a city within a city of palaces, courtyards and churches. Its centerpiece, St. Vitus Cathedral, dazzles with a stained-glass window by Alfons Mucha, and the tiny candy-colored cottages of Golden Lane once housed castle guards and, briefly, Franz Kafka's writing desk.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy the circuit ticket online and arrive before 9am, riding tram 22 up to the Pražský hrad stop to avoid the steep climb.

attractions.name: Charles Bridge
attractions.description: This cobbled 14th-century stone bridge is lined with thirty Baroque statues of saints, blackened by centuries of weather. By midday it's a gauntlet of painters and buskers, but at sunrise the mist over the Vltava and the castle silhouette make it pure magic.
attractions.bookingTip: Come before 7am for crowd-free photos, and climb the Old Town Bridge Tower for a small fee to see the bridge from above.

attractions.name: Old Town Square
attractions.description: The theatrical heart of the city, ringed by pastel Baroque façades, the twin dark spires of the Týn Church and the brooding Jan Hus memorial. It's a lovely spot to linger, though you'll eat and drink better a few streets away.
attractions.bookingTip: In December the square hosts the city's biggest Christmas market; the rest of the year, admire it from a quieter terrace on a side street.

attractions.name: Prague Astronomical Clock
attractions.description: Mounted on the Old Town Hall since 1410, this is the oldest astronomical clock still in operation, tracking the sun, moon and zodiac across its painted dial. On the hour a procession of apostles appears while a skeleton tolls the bell, and the tower above offers a sweeping view over the square.
attractions.hours: Show on the hour 09:00–23:00; tower approx. 09:00–21:00 (Mon from 11:00)
attractions.bookingTip: The hourly show lasts under a minute, so watch it once and then buy a tower ticket to look down on the crowds.

attractions.name: Josefov
attractions.description: Prague's former Jewish quarter preserves six synagogues and one of Europe's most haunting burial grounds, where thousands of tilting headstones crowd layer upon layer. Inside the Pinkas Synagogue, the walls are hand-lettered with the names of nearly 80,000 Czech and Moravian Jews murdered in the Holocaust.
attractions.hours: Jewish Museum sites 09:00–18:00 Sun–Fri (to 16:30 in winter), closed Sat and Jewish holidays
attractions.bookingTip: One combined ticket covers most synagogues and the cemetery; the Old-New Synagogue, still in active use, needs a separate or upgraded ticket.

attractions.name: Petřín Hill
attractions.description: A wooded hill above Malá Strana laced with orchards, rose gardens and footpaths, topped by a miniature Eiffel-style lookout tower from 1891. Climb the tower for a view over a hundred spires, then get happily lost in the old mirror maze next door.
attractions.hours: Park open 24 hours; lookout tower approx. 09:00–21:00
attractions.bookingTip: Walk up through the orchards from Újezd or ride the funicular when it's running, which accepts regular transit tickets; the tower and maze charge small fees.

attractions.name: Vyšehrad
attractions.description: Prague's other castle is a quieter, legend-steeped fortress on a cliff above the Vltava, with grassy ramparts, a twin-spired basilica and the cemetery where Dvořák and Mucha rest. Locals come for picnics and sunset views up the river toward the castle, far from the tour groups.
attractions.bookingTip: The grounds are free; pay a few dollars to tour the brick casemates, where several original Charles Bridge statues are kept safe.

attractions.name: Dancing House
attractions.description: Nicknamed Fred and Ginger, this curvy 1990s building by Frank Gehry and Vlado Milunić looks like a couple twirling on the riverbank. Its glass-walled rooftop bar is a fun spot for a drink with views over the Vltava to the castle.
attractions.hours: Exterior always visible; rooftop bar approx. 10:00–00:00
attractions.bookingTip: Admiring the façade is free, and the cheapest way onto the rooftop terrace is simply to order a drink at the bar.

attractions.name: Strahov Monastery
attractions.description: This hilltop abbey is famous for two Baroque library halls, the Theological and the Philosophical, with frescoed ceilings, antique globes and towering walnut shelves. The monastery also brews its own beer, and the orchard terraces below give one of the finest views over Prague's spires.
attractions.bookingTip: Visitors view the library halls from the doorways, so arrive early to get a clear look before the tour groups.

attractions.name: National Museum
attractions.description: The grand Neo-Renaissance museum crowns the top of Wenceslas Square, its gilded Pantheon hall lined with statues of Czech luminaries. Natural history collections sit alongside exhibits on the nation's past, and the dome looks down the square where the 1989 Velvet Revolution unfolded.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy online to skip the ticket desk, and don't miss the lift up into the dome for the view down Wenceslas Square.

hotels.name: U Stříbrné Lodičky
hotels.description: A cluster of Renaissance houses at the Malá Strana end of Charles Bridge, joined into a sumptuous hideaway with painted beams, a vaulted cellar spa and suites overlooking the river. From the garden terrace, the bridge statues stand silhouetted at sunset.

hotels.name: Dům U Zeleného Čápa
hotels.description: A medieval house with a green stork painted above the door, tucked down a lane two minutes from Old Town Square. Rooms pair Gothic vaulting with Czech modernist furniture, and breakfast features fresh koláče from a neighborhood bakery.
highlights: Two minutes to Old Town Square

hotels.name: Kavčí Hnízdo Hostel
hotels.description: A friendly hostel named for the jackdaw, the bird that gave Kafka his surname, set in a former printing house near the Jewish Quarter. Dorms are spotless, the basement bar pours cheap tank beer, and free walking tours leave every morning.

hotels.name: Hotel Rondokubus
hotels.description: A love letter to Czech Cubism and its rounded offshoot, rondocubism, with faceted mirrors, zigzag headboards and bold primary colors throughout. Riverfront rooms look toward the Dancing House and the castle.

hotels.name: Rezidence Hradní Sýpka
hotels.description: A converted 17th-century granary a short walk from the castle gates, with thick walls, timber beams and a courtyard garden where breakfast is served in summer. Once the day-trippers leave, the quiet lanes of Hradčany feel like a village.

hotels.name: Vinohrady Pavlač Apartments
hotels.description: Spacious apartments in an Art Nouveau tenement, reached by the traditional open-gallery walkways that ring a leafy inner courtyard. Vinohrady's cafés, wine bars and farmers' markets are on the doorstep, and trams reach the Old Town in minutes.

restaurants.name: Jíška
restaurants.description: In a vaulted Malá Strana cellar, a young chef reinvents grandmotherly recipes, turning svíčková into an elegant plate of aged beef and root-vegetable cream. The pairings champion Moravian wines and Czech craft ciders.

restaurants.name: Hospoda U Tančícího Medvěda
restaurants.description: A wood-paneled pub on the hill below the monastery, where waiters tally your beers on a paper slip and pork knuckle arrives on a wooden board. The roast duck with red cabbage and dumplings is worth the uphill walk.
restaurants.signatureDish: Roast duck with red cabbage and dumplings

restaurants.name: Kavárna Papírový Drak
restaurants.description: A book-lined café with mismatched chairs, where breakfast means fluffy scrambled eggs, poppy-seed koláče and excellent pour-over coffee. It's a peaceful refuge just off the busy Old Town streets.

restaurants.name: Chlebíčkárna Sedmikráska
restaurants.description: Czech chlebíčky, little open sandwiches piled with ham, egg, potato salad, beetroot or smoked fish, are lined up in a glass case like jewels. Point at a few, add a small beer and eat standing at the counter as locals do.
restaurants.signatureDish: Chlebíček with ham and potato salad

restaurants.name: Pivnice Pěna
restaurants.description: A bustling beer hall with long wooden tables, where unpasteurized tank lager arrives in thick glass mugs crowned with creamy foam. Soak it up with beef goulash and bread dumplings or a plate of crispy fried cheese.

restaurants.name: Bếp Nusle
restaurants.description: Prague's large Vietnamese community has made phở a city staple, and this simple canteen in the valley below Vyšehrad serves some of the best. Order bún chả with smoky grilled pork or fresh summer rolls stuffed with herbs.

restaurants.name: Hlubina Rybí Bistro
restaurants.description: A riverside bistro devoted to fish from South Bohemia's historic ponds, from crisp-skinned trout to the carp Czechs traditionally eat at Christmas. Big windows look out on swans and the embankment's Saturday farmers' market.

restaurants.name: Terasa U Třešní
restaurants.description: A garden restaurant tucked among cherry trees on the lower slopes of Petřín, with a terrace that looks across red roofs to the castle. The seasonal menu leans on game, forest mushrooms and Moravian wines.
restaurants.signatureDish: Venison with juniper sauce and potato dumplings

experiences.name: Vltava Twilight Boat with Bohemian Wine
experiences.description: Board a small wooden boat below Charles Bridge and drift past the castle, the river islands and the National Theatre as the city lights flicker on. A sommelier pours three Moravian wines with Czech cheeses along the way.

experiences.name: Hidden Beer Halls and Bites Tour
experiences.description: Duck into cellar pubs and microbreweries the crowds miss, tasting unpasteurized tank lager, dark beer and a craft IPA alongside classic pub food. Your guide decodes the rituals, from reading the tally slip to the three styles of pour.

experiences.name: Castle District at Dawn Photo Walk
experiences.description: Meet at first light, when the castle courtyards are empty, then wander down through Malá Strana's lanes to Charles Bridge before the crowds wake up. A local photographer shares composition tips and secret vantage points along the way.

experiences.name: Kutná Hora Bone Chapel Day Trip
experiences.description: Take the train from the main station beside the National Museum to the old silver-mining town of Kutná Hora, home to the Sedlec Ossuary, decorated with the bones of tens of thousands of people. The day continues at the soaring St. Barbara's Church with a traditional Czech lunch in between.
